findings.body: The workflow scan counts every job ID as a produced check, including jobs with an explicit different name. For example, if migration deletes a workflow producing `lint`, while a remaining workflow contains job ID `lint` with `name: frontend-lint`, `remaining` still contains `lint`. Consequently, the orphaned required check survives and blocks subsequent merges. GitHub distinguishes [job identifiers from job names](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-jobs). Use the effective check name, falling back to the ID only when appropriate, and extend the command-level migration test to cover named jobs.

findings.body: GitHub's [documented SSH-over-443 origin](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/troubleshooting-ssh/using-ssh-over-the-https-port), such as `ssh://git@ssh.github.com:443/acme/shop.git`, fails the hostname check and falls back to `{owner}/{repo}` for both API requests. Those [placeholders use gh's repository selection](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_api), restoring the wrong-repository risk with multiple remotes. Recognize this GitHub transport and fail explicitly for unresolved origins instead of silently restoring ambiguous selection.
findings.title: Keep SSH-over-443 origins bound to their repository

why: Forge's branch protection keeps required checks whose workflows a migration deletes, which blocks every later pull request once admins are enforced, and with two remotes and no gh default it can protect the wrong repo
